'''Brett John Hudson''' (born 1965)<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.parliament.nz/media/6305/roll-of-members-of-the-new-zealand-house-of-representatives-1854-onwards.pdf |title=Roll of members of the New Zealand House of Representatives, 1854 onwards |date=24 May 2019 |publisher=New Zealand Parliament |accessdate=3 September 2020}}</ref> is a New Zealand politician who was a Member of Parliament for the [[New Zealand National Party]] from 2014 to 2020.

==Early life==
Born to Alfred "Rocky" Hudson, and his wife – Jantzen Swimwear factory machinist Carol – Hudson's family moved to Porirua in 1972. Hudson attended Porirua East School, Tītahi Bay Intermediate School, and Mana College.<ref>[https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/51HansS_20141029_00000972/hudson-brett-address-in-reply Address in Reply Debate (Maiden Speech) Brett Hudson] 29 October 2014, accessed 27 January 2024 [https://www.parliament.nz/ New Zealand Parliament Website – Hansard]</ref>

Hudson undertook tertiary study at [[Victoria University of Wellington|Victoria University]], graduating in 1990 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in History and Psychology.<ref>[https://www.linkedin.com/in/brett-hudson-nz Personal profile: Brett Hudson] accessed 27 January 2024 [[LinkedIn]]</ref>

Immediately prior to entering politics, Hudson had a career in information technology, working in business development, contracting, sales and account management for major international firms such as [[IBM]], [[Oracle Corporation|Oracle]], and [[TelstraClear|Telstra-Clear]] – as well as New Zealand-owned consultancy StarFish.<ref>[https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1405/S00003/national-selects-brett-hudson-as-ohariu-candidate.htm Press Release: National Selects Brett Hudson for Ohariu] 1 May 2014 [https://www.scoop.co.nz Scoop Press Releases]</ref>

Hudson stood in the [[2011 New Zealand general election|2011 election]], but his rank of 73rd on [[New Zealand National Party|National's]] party list meant he was not elected to Parliament. In [[2014 New Zealand general election|2014 election]] the National Party selected him to contest [[Ōhāriu (New Zealand electorate)|Ōhāriu]] against incumbent [[Peter Dunne]] of the [[United Future]] Party.<ref>{{cite news |title=Today in Politics: Thursday, May 1 |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/dominion-post/news/politics/9994828/Today-in-Politics-Thursday-May-1 |accessdate=22 October 2020 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=30 April 2014 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809090310/http://www.stuff.co.nz/dominion-post/news/politics/9994828/Today-in-Politics-Thursday-May-1 |archivedate=9 August 2017}}</ref> While unsuccessful in his electorate, he was ranked 39th on National's 2014 party list, enough to become a list MP.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Trevett |first1=Claire |title=National releases list of candidates |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11299883 |accessdate=22 October 2020 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=27 July 2014 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170809041919/http://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11299883 |archivedate=9 August 2017}}</ref>

In opposition, Hudson was appointed as his party's Spokesperson for Police, Commerce and Consumer Affairs, Government Digital Services, and Associate Spokesperson for Transport in [[Simon Bridges|Simon Bridges']] [[Shadow Cabinet of Simon Bridges|shadow cabinet]] 2018–20. Hudson retained the Police and Government Digital Services portfolios through the leaderships of Bridges' successors [[Shadow Cabinet of Todd Muller|Todd Muller]] and [[Shadow Cabinet of Judith Collins|Judith Collins]].

At the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 election's]] landslide result against National, Hudson lost Ōhāriu by nearly 12,000 votes, and was not placed high enough on National's list to return to Parliament as a list MP.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Ōhāriu – Official Result|url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-33.html|access-date=13 November 2020|website=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Whyte |first1=Anna |title=Analysis: The winners, losers, new faces and goodbyes of election 2020 |url=https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/analysis-winners-losers-new-faces-and-goodbyes-election-2020 |accessdate=22 October 2020 |work=[[1News]] |date=18 October 2020 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022090204/https://www.tvnz.co.nz/one-news/new-zealand/analysis-winners-losers-new-faces-and-goodbyes-election-2020 |archivedate=22 October 2020}}</ref>

===Political positions===

During his time in Parliament, Hudson marked himself out as a social liberal on conscience issues, by voting in favour of legislation that: decriminalised abortion; set up a referendum to enable euthanasia; and allowed territorial authorities to decide whether to permit Easter opening in their respective districts. Hudson supported all three measures in each of the three readings of the bill.<ref>[https://voted.nz/people/hudson-brett/ Voted – Brett Hudson, National List MP] accessed 27 January 2024 [https://voted.nz/about/ Voted: Vote Tracker]</ref>

Hudson was more conservative when it came to law and order measures. He voted against cannabis liberalisation in January 2018 (in line with caucus colleagues), and supported the introduction of an Australian-inspired, '[[Strike Force Raptor]]'-style, anti-gang squad while he was Police Spokesperson in 2019.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20191127213313/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2019/11/national-ponders-strike-force-raptor-police-unit-to-harass-gangs-in-policy-proposal.html National ponders 'Strike Force Raptor' police unit to 'harass gangs' in policy proposal] 26 November 2019 [[Newshub]]</ref>

==After politics==

Following his exit from Parliament, Hudson relocated to Dunedin and returned to study in economics. He has served on the board of recreational and environmental charity the [[Waitaki District|Waitaki]] Whitestone Geopark Trust – a [[UNESCO Global Geoparks|UNESCO Global Geopark]] – since September 2021.<ref>[https://www.whitestonegeopark.nz/post/waitaki-whitestone-geopark-trust-announces-new-chair Waitaki Whitestone Geopark Trust Announces New Chair] 27 September 2021 [https://www.whitestonegeopark.nz/the-trust Whitestone Geopark]</ref>

Hudson also serves as Chair of the Audit and Risk Committee on the board of [http://www.able.org.nz/ Able Minds], a mental health charity that seeks to support those suffering from distress and addicition, and their families and [[whānau]].<ref>[http://www.able.org.nz/our%20people.html Able Minds – Our People] Accessed 27 January 2024</ref>

==Personal life==

Hudson is partnered with IT professional Lindsay Renwick, and has three adult daughters from a previous marriage.<ref>[https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1405/S00003/national-selects-brett-hudson-as-ohariu-candidate.htm Press Release: National Selects Brett Hudson for Ohariu] 1 May 2014 [https://www.scoop.co.nz Scoop Press Releases]</ref>

For recreation, Hudson enjoys road cycling and motorcycling.<ref>[https://www.policeassn.org.nz/news/ten-questions-with#/ 10 Questions with... Police Spokesperson Brett Hudson] 1 August 2019 [[New Zealand Police Association|NZ Police Association]] Newsletter</ref>
